## Exact assumptions and conditional bounds

- [`sat26-sparse`](../../ASSUMPTIONS.md#sat26-sparse)
- [`sat26-reported-formal`](../../ASSUMPTIONS.md#sat26-reported-formal)

Conditional on `sat26-sparse`:

$$
2^{O(k/\sqrt{\log k})}L^{O(1)}
$$

Alternatively, conditional on `sat26-reported-formal`:

$$
2^{O(k(\log\log k)^2/\sqrt{\log k})}L^{O(1)}
$$

The resulting algorithm is deterministic and uses polynomial space, conditional on the corresponding assumption and this derivation. $L$ denotes the original input length; constants may depend on the stated fixed constants. Logarithms in asymptotic bounds may be regularized when the declared measure is small.

## Preprocessing

If |V| > (Δ+1)k, return NO; otherwise |V|=O_Δ(k).

## Encoding size

| Quantity | Bound |
| --- | --- |
| Boolean variables, including auxiliaries | $O_{\Delta}(k)$ |
| Clauses | $O_{\Delta}(k)$ |
| Maximum clause width | $\max\{\Delta+1,3\}$ |

## Derivation

1. A set of k vertices dominates at most (Δ+1)k vertices. On the remaining instance, impose $\bigvee_{u\in N[v]}x_u$ for each vertex v.

2. Add the linear-size encoding of $\sum_v x_v\le k$. Clause width is at most max(Δ+1,3), and both variables and clauses are O_Δ(k), giving the sparse bound.

## Caveats and comparison limits

- This is bounded maximum degree, not an assertion about unrestricted Dominating Set parameterized by solution size.

A decision-preserving kernel does not automatically preserve the number of solutions.
